item.title: Weiser readies for volunteer challenge, Serve Day
item.description: Idaho will mark America’s 250th birthday with a year of volunteerism and Weiser plans to join in the public service party. Serve Day, an annual volunteer event organized by Ontario non-profit Better Together Inc., is already slated for April 25. In addition, America250 ambassador Nikki Dale urged residents to help achieve Idaho lawmakers’ goal of completing 250,000 acts of service before July 4. item.title: School district considering bus tracking system
item.description: The Weiser School District board postponed a decision on adopting BusRight, a bus tracking and student ridership system, after an in depth discussion during its March 9 meeting. Board members and administrators expressed interest in the system’s potential to improve communication, safety, and operational efficiency, but agreed more information is needed before moving forward. item.title: Vaughn joins Weiser City Council
item.description: Joseph Vaughn was appointed to the Weiser City Council to replace Herb Haun. Photo by D. Brown Joe Vaughn slotted seamlessly onto the Weiser City Council in March, even if it was a few months later than he had hoped. Vaughn was appointed by Mayor Herb Haun to fill the council seat that Haun vacated in order to replace former Mayor Randy Hibberd, who resigned in January due to health issues. item.title: WAPC hosts Declaration talk March 25
item.description: In celebration of America250, the Weiser Architectural Preservation Committee (WAPC) will host nationally recognized constitutional scholar Dr. David Gray Adler for a public lecture on the Declaration of Independence on March 25 at 6 p.m. at the historic Weiser Train Depot. Supported by the Idaho Humanities Council, the event highlights Weiser’s long tradition of civic learning and community pride. item.title: Fast start for Weiser track at Ice Breaker
item.description: Pictured in a heat of the 100-meters at the Parma Ice Breaker on Friday, March 13, are from left, Wolverines Alex Juarez and Gabe McLaughlin, and Tri-Valley Titan Bill Avery. Weiser High School just had its first track and field meet of the season on March 13 at Parma High School. The WHS track team has already been practicing and working hard for the first few weeks of March. All that work started to pay off at the Parma Ice Breaker.
